# Previews: next steps

Generated by `patchy setup previews` (patchy v0.12.40) for the **tailnet device (Tailscale operator)** recipe on **k3d**.
Previews will be served at `https://<project>-<issue>.acme-previews.dev`, and viewers sign in at `https://preview-auth.patchy.acme.dev`.
Nothing here has been applied: run the steps below in order. Running `patchy setup previews` again shows what would
change before it replaces a file, and never draws a new Dex client secret unless you pass
`--rotate dex-client-secret`.

## Files

| File | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `NEXT-STEPS.md` | This file. |
| `answers.yaml` | Every answer, the edge and the CLI version: a re-run starts from it. No secret. |
| `manifests/certificate.yaml` | The cert-manager Certificate for `*.<suffix>` and the sign-in host. |
| `manifests/issuer.yaml` | The ACME Issuer that answers the Certificate's DNS-01 challenge (a ClusterIssuer when cert-manager's own identity answers). |
| `patchy-previews.values.yaml` | patchy's chart values for previews, layered after your own. |
| `secrets/dex-patchy-preview-auth-client.secret.yaml` | The same secret, in Dex's namespace, for its static client (0600). |
| `secrets/patchy-preview-auth-dex.secret.yaml` | The relay's Dex client secret, in the release namespace (0600). |
| `secrets/preview-dns01-credentials.secret.yaml` | The DNS-01 solver's credential, in the release namespace (0600). |
| `upstream/cert-manager.values.yaml` | cert-manager's values, for the chart version patchy pins (v1.21.2). |
| `upstream/tailscale-operator.values.yaml` | The Tailscale operator's values, for the chart version patchy pins (1.104.1). |

The files under `secrets/` (mode 0600) hold the only copy of the Dex client secret and of
the DNS credential you gave. Apply them, or encrypt them (sops,
sealed-secrets) before they go anywhere else; never commit them as they are.

## 1. Before you start

- patchy is installed in namespace `patchy` as release `patchy`, with `intentController.enabled: true`
  in your values: previews are built for intents, and the preview-controller needs intent-controller.
- NetworkPolicy is enforced. k3s enforces it with its embedded kube-router unless the server runs with `--disable-network-policy`.
- cert-manager is installed in step 5 from `upstream/cert-manager.values.yaml` (chart v1.21.2),
  unless it already runs: then run the command again with `--cert-manager-installed`.
- The Tailscale operator is installed in step 6 from `upstream/tailscale-operator.values.yaml` (chart
  1.104.1), unless it already runs: then run the command again with
  `--tailscale-operator-installed`.

## 2. Preview nodes

Every slot Pod selects `patchy.bitwisemedia.uk/previews=true` and tolerates the taint `patchy.bitwisemedia.uk/preview-only=true:NoExecute`. Add at least one node with both, set when it registers so no other Pod lands on it first.

```sh
k3d node create preview --cluster <cluster> --role agent --k3s-node-label patchy.bitwisemedia.uk/previews=true \
  --k3s-arg "--node-taint=patchy.bitwisemedia.uk/preview-only=true:NoExecute"
```

`patchy-previews.values.yaml` sets `preview.nodeIsolation` over your own values, but Helm merges its `selector` map: remove any `preview.nodeIsolation.selector` from your own values, or Pods require those labels too.

On one host this isolates scheduling only: the preview node shares the host's kernel.

## 3. Preview image pulls

Preview images are `123456789012.dkr.ecr.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/patchy/previews/<app>:sha-<commit>`. Slot Pods may not reference a Secret, so pulls are
the node's own: a private registry needs credentials on the preview nodes only: k3s's `registries.yaml` (`configs."123456789012.dkr.ecr.us-east-1.amazonaws.com".auth`) or a kubelet credential provider, with a key that can pull `patchy/previews/*` and nothing else. Public images need nothing, but make preview images of private code public only knowingly.

## 4. Dex

Add the relay's static client to Dex's configuration, with its one redirect URI:

```yaml
staticClients:
  - id: patchy-preview-auth
    name: patchy previews
    secretEnv: PATCHY_PREVIEW_AUTH_CLIENT_SECRET
    redirectURIs:
      - https://preview-auth.patchy.acme.dev/dex/callback
```

Give Dex the secret in that environment variable from the Secret in its namespace (with Dex's Helm chart:
`envVars: [{name: PATCHY_PREVIEW_AUTH_CLIENT_SECRET, valueFrom: {secretKeyRef: {name: patchy-preview-auth-client, key: clientSecret}}}]`),
then roll Dex:

```sh
kubectl apply -f secrets/dex-patchy-preview-auth-client.secret.yaml
```

## 5. TLS

The gateway terminates TLS itself with one certificate for `*.acme-previews.dev` and `preview-auth.patchy.acme.dev`, issued by cert-manager
and picked up again at every renewal without a restart.

Install cert-manager at the version patchy pins:

```sh
helm upgrade --install cert-manager cert-manager --repo https://charts.jetstack.io \
  --version v1.21.2 -n cert-manager --create-namespace -f upstream/cert-manager.values.yaml
```

The Issuer answers the challenge with the `route53` DNS-01 solver. Grant the IAM user whose access key you give this policy and nothing else: only TXT records, only the two challenge names, in only the zones that hold them.

```json
{
  "Version": "2012-10-17",
  "Statement": [
    {
      "Sid": "AcmeChallengeRecordsOnly",
      "Effect": "Allow",
      "Action": ["route53:ChangeResourceRecordSets"],
      "Resource": [
        "arn:aws:route53:::hostedzone/<the zone holding acme-previews.dev>",
        "arn:aws:route53:::hostedzone/<the zone holding preview-auth.patchy.acme.dev>"
      ],
      "Condition": {
        "ForAllValues:StringEquals": {
          "route53:ChangeResourceRecordSetsNormalizedRecordNames": [
            "_acme-challenge.acme-previews.dev",
            "_acme-challenge.preview-auth.patchy.acme.dev"
          ],
          "route53:ChangeResourceRecordSetsRecordTypes": ["TXT"],
          "route53:ChangeResourceRecordSetsActions": ["UPSERT", "DELETE"]
        }
      }
    },
    {
      "Sid": "ChangeStatus",
      "Effect": "Allow",
      "Action": ["route53:GetChange"],
      "Resource": "arn:aws:route53:::change/*"
    },
    {
      "Sid": "FindZone",
      "Effect": "Allow",
      "Action": ["route53:ListHostedZonesByName"],
      "Resource": "*"
    }
  ]
}
```

Its credential is in `secrets/preview-dns01-credentials.secret.yaml`:

```sh
kubectl apply -f secrets/preview-dns01-credentials.secret.yaml
```

```sh
kubectl apply -f manifests/issuer.yaml
kubectl apply -f manifests/certificate.yaml
kubectl -n patchy wait certificate/preview-wildcard --for=condition=Ready --timeout=10m
```

`previewAuth.gateway.tls.secrets` names its Secret, `preview-wildcard-tls`. The two names sit on different
registrable domains, so usually in two DNS zones: the solver must be able to answer for both.

## 6. Install

The gateway's device joins the tailnet through the Tailscale operator. In the tailnet policy, let the operator own the
previews' tag and let viewers reach that device on 443 alone (put whoever views previews in `group:preview-viewers`;
each still signs in):

```json
{
  "tagOwners": {
    "tag:k8s-operator": ["autogroup:admin"],
    "tag:patchy-previews": ["tag:k8s-operator"]
  },
  "grants": [
    {
      "src": ["group:preview-viewers"],
      "dst": ["tag:patchy-previews"],
      "ip": ["tcp:443"]
    }
  ]
}
```

Create an OAuth client in the Tailscale admin console with the write scopes the operator's guide
(https://tailscale.com/kb/1236/kubernetes-operator) names, tagged `tag:k8s-operator`. Put its ID and secret
in two files, never on a command line, then:

```sh
kubectl create namespace tailscale
kubectl -n tailscale create secret generic operator-oauth \
  --from-file=client_id=<the client ID's file> --from-file=client_secret=<the client secret's file>
helm upgrade --install tailscale-operator tailscale-operator --repo https://pkgs.tailscale.com/helmcharts \
  --version 1.104.1 -n tailscale -f upstream/tailscale-operator.values.yaml
```

Then patchy:

```sh
kubectl apply -f secrets/patchy-preview-auth-dex.secret.yaml
helm upgrade patchy oci://ghcr.io/devthenet-labs/patchy/charts/patchy -n patchy --version 0.12.40 \
  -f <your values> -f patchy-previews.values.yaml
```

One upgrade: the gateway needs no permit stage. `previewController.config.apiServerCIDR: auto` is looked up at render time, so it needs `helm upgrade` against the cluster (not
`helm template` or a GitOps render, which must set the kubernetes Service's `/32` instead).

## 7. DNS

Point two records at the edge's address:

- `*.acme-previews.dev`
- `preview-auth.patchy.acme.dev`

The address is the tailnet device `patchy-previews`'s, once the operator has created it (`tailscale ip -4
patchy-previews` on any machine in the tailnet, or the admin console). MagicDNS takes no wildcard or custom
records, so these are records in your public DNS that point at a tailnet address: only the tailnet can reach it. You gave `100.101.12.58`
(`previewAuth.gateway.publishedAddresses`, which `patchy check previews` compares DNS with).

The gateway sees the tailnet proxy's address, not the viewer's, so `previewAuth.gateway.forwardedHops` is 0 and
`inboundCIDRs` stays empty: the tailnet policy above is the allowlist.

## 8. Check

```sh
patchy check previews -n patchy
```

Every line should PASS before the first intent's preview is opened.

## Rolling back

In reverse order, all by deletion:

1. Set `previewAuth.gateway.enabled: false` (or `preview.enabled: false`) and run the same `helm upgrade`.
2. `kubectl delete -f manifests/certificate.yaml` and `kubectl delete -f manifests/issuer.yaml`, then remove the device `patchy-previews` from the tailnet if
   the operator has not.
3. Remove the two DNS records.
4. Remove the static client from Dex, and delete the Secrets (`kubectl delete -f secrets/`).
   Uninstall what this recipe installed if nothing else uses it: `helm uninstall
   tailscale-operator -n tailscale`, `helm uninstall cert-manager -n cert-manager` (its CRDs stay, and
   with them every Certificate in the cluster).
5. Delete what the chart keeps on uninstall, as `docs/intents/preview-sign-in.md` lists it.
